effectiveNote: PIPA 37-2 (rights regarding automated decisions) in force from 2024-03-15 (Act 19234 addendum 1(1)).

rules.statement: State that automated decisions are made (fully automated systems, including AI), their specific purpose, and which data subjects are affected, so they know they can exercise rights.
State the main types of personal data used and how they relate to the decision; types may be given instead of every item.
State what the data subject should know about the decision process and the procedure by which the main data is processed.
If sensitive data or data of children under 14 is processed in the decision, state the purpose and specific items in advance (or state that none is processed).
State that the data subject may refuse or request an explanation (and review), and the method and procedure.
Use standardized terms and visual aids (diagrams, charts, video) for AI-based processing.

goodPatterns: Five headed blocks in the order of the checklist (fact/purpose/scope; data types and weight in the decision; process and considerations; sensitive/child data; refusal, explanation and review requests with department, contact and procedure).
Examples in the guideline: AI hiring with stage weights; AI detection of improper welfare payments with a step flow.

commonDefects.defect: Automated rejection or sanction exists but no S17 section.
No method or procedure to refuse or request explanation.
Data types listed without their relation to the decision.

manualReview: Whether a decision is 'fully automated' and whether refusal is excluded (consent, contract notice, statute) is a legal judgment; always emit a manual_review note.

needsVerification.note: Reply deadlines (10 days refusal, 30 days action) and refusal exclusions appear only in the guideline examples; the governing decree article is not cited in the guideline.
